lyrics:
[Intro: slide guitar, floor-tom groove, handclaps]

[Verse 1: raspy male voice, storytelling]
Danny couldn't walk since the accident in June
We heard a man was in town, said he might be leaving soon
House was packed out to the street, couldn't get in the door
So Marcus looked at me and said, "What's a roof for?"

[Chorus: gang vocals, full band, anthemic]
We cut a hole in the roof
Four friends and a rope and a mat
Dust coming down on the good people's heads
We weren't sorry about that
When a friend can't get there on his own
You carry him, you make a way through
You don't knock, you don't wait, you don't ask
You cut a hole in the roof

[Verse 2: voice lower, band holding back]
We lowered him down in the middle of the room
Right at the feet of Jesus, in the quiet, in the gloom
He looked up at us four, sweating, through the beams
Then down at Danny, smiling: "Son, you're forgiven. You're free."

[Chorus: gang vocals, full band, anthemic]
We cut a hole in the roof
Four friends and a rope and a mat
Dust coming down on the good people's heads
We weren't sorry about that
When a friend can't get there on his own
You carry him, you make a way through
You don't knock, you don't wait, you don't ask
You cut a hole in the roof

[Bridge: half-time, organ, building]
Then he said, "Get up," and Danny did
Walked out the front door carrying his bed
I've been the one on the mat since then
And I've had friends on the rope. Amen.

[Final Chorus: loudest, everyone]
So we'll cut a hole in the roof
Four friends and a rope and a mat
If you can't get to him on your own
We will carry you. Count on that.
When a friend can't get there by himself
You carry him, you make a way through
You don't knock, you don't wait, you don't ask
You cut a hole in the roof

[Outro: slide guitar, hammering, laughter]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 100 BPM, 4/4, A major. A rolling Southern roots-rock groove with a big, swinging backbeat.

VOICE: Male baritone, raspy and warm, telling the story with relish. A gang of men sing every chorus with him, loud and a little ragged. The bridge is quieter and wondering.

INSTRUMENTS: Slide guitar, a floor-tom and kick groove with handclaps, overdriven rhythm guitar, bass, Hammond organ, piano pounding eighth notes in the chorus, tambourine, a banjo low in the mix.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, slide guitar and toms. 0:12 Verse 1. 0:38 Chorus 1. 1:06 Verse 2, the room below. 1:34 Chorus 2. 2:02 Bridge, half-time. 2:26 Final chorus. 2:56 Outro, slide guitar, hammering and laughter, ends 3:16.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-2010s Southern rock: warm, live, guitars and organ thick, gang vocals wide.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: '"What's a roof for?"' at 0:34, straight into the gang chorus.

THE REVEAL: Verse 1 and the first chorus are four friends doing something reckless for a fifth. Verse 2 at 1:06 puts Jesus in the room below, in the words of Mark chapter 2, and the bridge has the man walk out.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Determined, daring, astonished, sworn to each other.
